question: Why did treating wild wombats for mange need a drug that stays in the body for weeks?
answer: Because a wild wombat can rarely be dosed twice. Ivermectin and moxidectin clear from wombat blood fast, so one dose often fails to kill every mite. Fluralaner, sold as a dog flea treatment, lingers for weeks; in trials a single dose cleared mild to moderate mange within about four weeks.
move: Choose the remedy that works on the only chance you will get.
